html.<b>この順番で測ると、ホーンを外さずに「線か・部品か」が分かれます。</b>②: Measure in this order and you can tell “wire or part” without removing the horn. The most common pattern is 12V at ② that doesn't drop at ③ (inside the column and the button contacts are where things move most and wear out).
html.<b>ヒューズ F1 か紫の線</b>。⭐ここで<b>ルームランプを点けてみてく: Fuse F1 or the purple wire. ⭐ Now try switching on the interior light — it's after the same F1. If the interior light is off too, it's the fuse. If the interior light comes on, it's the single purple wire
html.<b>ヒューズ F1 を通ります。</b>⚠️第4回ではこのヒューズを<b>横に: Through fuse F1. ⚠️ In Part 4 this fuse was drawn as a branch hanging off to the side, because the red wire to the key branches off before the fuse. The horn is after the fuse — so this time the main line runs vertically through it.
html.<b>ホーンの紫の線は、キーを抜いても生きています。</b>この線はヒューズ F:
The horn's purple wire stays live even with the key out. It's after fuse F1 = a circuit fed from the battery all the time. Before touching the wiring, disconnect the battery's negative (−) terminal. Let a tool touch the body and it short-circuits straight away.
⚠️ If the horn gets stuck on, disconnecting the battery's negative terminal also comes first (if a wire touches ground in the button or the column, it keeps sounding without being pressed). A horn sounding continuously gets hot.
⚠️ The 500's horn circuit has no relay (there is none in the original wiring diagram). The horn current goes straight through the thin button contact inside the steering wheel — which is why it wears.
html.<b>ボタンを押している＝帰り道がつながって、ホーンが鳴っています。</b>注目: Button pressed = the way back is connected and the horn sounds. Note that the key is still OFF. The horn always has 12V; the button doesn't “send” current, it just drops it to ground and closes the loop. That's why the horn sounds even with the key out.
html.<b>ボタンを離した＝帰り道が切れました。</b>ホーンのプラス端子にはこの瞬間: Button released = the way back is cut. The horn's positive terminal still has 12V at this moment (which is why the wire keeps its colour). Voltage is there, but it doesn't sound — that's the normal state. Put a meter on it and you read 12V on both horn terminals.
html.<span class=\"pin-hot\">●</span>ヒューズ箱も<s: Both the ● fuse box and the ● horn are at the front of the car. The horn sits behind the front panel (inside the grille), the spot that takes the most rain and mud. Corroded terminals and a rusty ground are the most common causes of this symptom.
html.<span class=\"qa-h\">なぜスイッチが「帰り道」側に付いている: Why is the switch on the “way back” side? The steering wheel turns. Running a ground wire through something that turns is safer than running a 12V wire (if it chafes and touches the body, the horn just sounds). For the same reason, the oil pressure warning light (Part 2) is also grounded at the sender.
html.F1 が切れたところ。ヒューズから<b>下が丸ごと薄く</b>なりました。第1回: F1 blown. Everything below the fuse has faded. In Parts 1, 4 and 6 we kept saying “checking the fuse won't fix it”, but that was about circuits that branch off before the fuse. The horn is after the fuse. And the fuse that blows is not the key-ON F2 that was the culprit in Parts 7, 10 and 11, but F1, which is live regardless of the key.
html.② ボタンを<b>押さずに</b>、<b>ホーンのマイナス端子</b>を測る: ② Without pressing the button, measure the horn's negative terminal
html.③ <b>ボタンを押しながら</b>、もう一度マイナス端子を測る: ③ While pressing the button, measure the negative terminal again
html.⚠️<b>ヒューズを替えたら、また切れた</b>ときは、替えるのをやめて原因を探: ⚠️ If the new fuse blows again, stop replacing it and look for the cause. It blows because the purple or yellow/black wire is touching ground somewhere, and the fuse is taking the hit in its place. Fit a bigger fuse and the next thing to burn is the wire.
html.⚠️<span class=\"pin-sub\">●</span><b>ホーン: ⚠️ ● The horn button mark points to the centre of the steering wheel. The button itself is at the end of a wire that comes down through the column, so its position can't be shown as a single point on a map seen from above.
html.⭐<b>F1 の先にいるのは、ホーンとルームランプの2つだけ</b>です（原典の: ⭐ Only two things are after F1: the horn and the interior light (the original fuse table). So “horn silent + interior light off too” is almost always explained by one fuse. Conversely, the charge lamp, the starter and the ignition all live independently of F1 — in this diagram you can see that from the wire to the key branching off before the fuse.
html.⭐<b>純正の整備解説書は、「ホーンが鳴らない」の原因を6つ挙げています</b>:
⭐ The factory workshop manual lists six causes of “horn doesn't sound” — ① blown fuse ② broken or loose wiring ③ ⭐ dirt or wear on the ring-shaped contact at the centre of the steering wheel ④ faulty button contact ⑤ bad ground on the horn itself ⑥ worn contacts or misadjustment inside the horn.
⭐ ③ is a place this diagram can't draw. The button turns with the wheel, so a ring contact that keeps touching as it turns is used to pass current to it. It wears the most, yet it's the hardest to see — if you get stuck at ③ in the table above, this is the next thing to open.
html.このストーリーは <b>FIAT 500（D・F・L・R型）</b> の話です。: This story is about the FIAT 500 (D, F, L and R). The wiring is taken from the 500's original sources.

html.キーは OFF のまま、ボタンを押しただけです。<b>紫の線を降りてきた電気が、: The key is still OFF; we just pressed the button. Current comes down the purple wire, through the horn's winding, up the column and to ground at the button — the moment this loop closes, it sounds.
html.ヒューズと紫の線は<b>生きている</b> → ②へ: The fuse and purple wire are live → go to ②
html.ヒューズを出た<b>紫の線（VIOLA）</b>が、ホーンのプラス（＋）端子まで: Leaving the fuse, the purple wire (VIOLA) brings 12V to the horn's positive (+) terminal. Up to here it's always live, regardless of the key.
html.ホーンの<b>内部が断線</b>しています（この絵には出てきません＝部品の中の話: Broken inside the horn (not shown in this diagram = it's inside the part)
html.ホーンのマイナス端子から出た<b>黄／黒の線</b>がステアリングコラムを通り、: From the horn's negative terminal, the yellow/black wire runs through the steering column to the horn button. Press the button and it drops to the body (ground) there, closing the loop.
html.ホーンの中の巻線が<b>つながっている</b>証拠です（電圧が巻線を通り抜けて向: Proof that the winding inside the horn is intact (the voltage shows through the winding to the other side) → go to ③
html.ボタンから先が切れています。<b>コラムの中の黄／黒線・ボタンの接点・ボタンのア: It's broken from the button onwards: the yellow/black wire in the column, the button contact, the button ground. Measuring while turning the steering wheel a little can reveal a break inside the column
html.ボタンのアースが外れたところ。ホーンのプラスにもマイナスにも12Vが来ていて、線: The button ground has come off. Both the horn's positive and negative have 12V, and the wires keep their colour. Even so no current flows — there's no way back.
html.ボタンは押されている。<b>キーの位置は関係ありません</b>——鍵を抜いた状態: The button is pressed. The key position doesn't matter — on a 500 the horn should sound even with the key out. Yet there's no sound: that's the symptom on this page.
html.ボタンを押しても、うんともすんとも言わない。——ホーンの回路は、ここまでたどって: You press the button and get nothing at all. — The horn circuit is the opposite in two ways of the routes we've followed so far. One: it's live without turning the key. Two: the switch sits on the way-back side.
html.上の表の③で「12V のまま」がこれです。<b>どこを測っても電圧が出るのに何も: This is “stays at 12V” at ③ in the table above. Voltage wherever you measure, yet nothing happens — this shape also appeared in Part 6 (ignition primary). Electricity depends not only on “does it arrive” but on “can it get back”: the backbone shared by all the parts so far (→ Part 5).
html.帰り道は正常＝<b>電気の道は全部つながっています</b>。それでも鳴らないなら: The way back is fine = the whole electrical path is connected. If it still won't sound, it's the horn itself (adjusting screw, worn internal contacts)
html.期待値は原典（純正取扱説明書の配線図）と実車の挙動から先に書いたもので、計算結果: The expected values were written first, from the original (the factory owner's handbook wiring diagram) and the real car's behaviour, not copied from the calculation. Even one ✗ means the diagram's data is wrong. ⭐ The first row, “key OFF, press the button and it sounds”, anyone can check on a real car — that it matches is the evidence that the horn is on the always-live 30 circuit.
html.測る場所は<b>ホーンのプラス端子</b>と<b>マイナス端子</b>の2つ。テ: There are two places to measure: the horn's positive terminal and its negative terminal. Put the meter's black lead on the battery's negative terminal. The key can stay OFF.
html.線の色は実車の被覆の色そのまま（VIOLA=紫・GIALLO E NERO=黄／: Wire colours are the real insulation colours (VIOLA = purple, GIALLO E NERO = yellow/black, NERO = black). Yellow dots = where current is flowing now. The round tags on the wires are terminal names. The dark tags are the two places we'll put the meter on = the horn's + and −. The winding inside the horn is drawn as a thin light line — it's the inside of a part, not a wire in the original. Only the terminal after the fuse says “(no name)” — because it has no name in the original wiring diagram, and on the real car you won't find a number there either.
